_what: Audited, attributed changes to a baseline-recorded count. checkpoint.py treats a MATCHING entry as expected rather than as drift, and still FAILS on any unlisted change. This exists so that correcting a number that was WRONG does not require either rewriting a frozen baseline or disabling the comparison -- both of which would destroy the evidence the comparison provides.
_rules: An amendment records from/to and WHY, with the evidence that settled it.
It never edits a frozen snapshot. The baseline keeps saying 252; this file explains why 242 is right.
An unlisted count change still halts the stop. This is not an override flag.
One entry per correction. If a count changes twice, that is two entries, and the chain must connect.

axioms_pinned.reason: 10 of the 252 were COMPILER BACKEND ARTIFACTS, not trust assumptions: lambda-lifted fields of structure-instance defs (intModel._elambda_1..5, emlEmptyChain._elambda_1..2, two SDR-solver _elambda_1s, twoExpLowerReductionSolver_of_predicateSolver._elambda_1). The code generator emits them as genuinely .axiomInfo constants, so liveAxioms' prefix filter swept them in. v4.23.0's compiler stopped emitting them, which is what made the ledger's rot check fire.
evidence: All 10 were .axiomInfo at v4.20.1 -- observed directly in a git-worktree rebuild of tag toolchain-stop/v4.20.1, not inferred from the filter.
Their types are code-generation shapes: Int -> Int, Int -> Int -> Int, Fin 0 -> MultiPoly 0, Fin 0 -> Real -> Real.
ZERO of the 57 headline footprints ever cited one, across all six frozen snapshots (v4.14.0 baseline, v4.16.0, v4.19.0, v4.19.0-r2, v4.20.1, v4.23.0).
ZERO real declarations cite one: all 17 transitive citers under MachLib are _cstage1/_cstage2/_closed_N._cstage2 compiler IR artifacts.
So no mathematics ever depended on them, and 242 was the honest count of user-declared trust assumptions all along.
axioms_pinned.structural_fix: liveAxioms (AxiomLedger.lean) and emit_ledger.py now both exclude compiler artifacts by name predicate, so the miscount is unrepresentable rather than merely corrected. Deleting ten list entries alone would have left the next compiler-emitted axiom-shaped closure free to walk back in.
axioms_pinned.not_a_drift: No axiom was added to or removed from the trust boundary by the migration. The DESCRIPTION was wrong; the boundary did not move. This is a finding the bump surfaced, not damage the bump caused.
